lawyer:
Md. Abdun Nur Advocate ----- For the Petitioner.
Md. Abdul Awal, Advocate ----- For the Respondent Nos. 2-4.
parties:
Bangladesh Development Bank Limited ------ Petitioner 
Vs.
Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Jessore and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Ashfaqul Islam J: At the instance of the petitioner, Bangladesh Development Bank Limited, this Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondent Nos. l to 4 to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 25-9-2011 passed by the Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Jessore in Artha Rin Suit No. 83 of 2004 and judgment and order dated 13-11-2011 passed by the Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Jessore in Artha Jari Case No. 9 of 2005 shall not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 3. The petitioner-bank then filed Artha Jari Case No. 9 of 2005 in the Adalat and in due compliance of law got a certificate under section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as Ain). Subsequently one of the Director, namely, Abul Kalam Azad filed applications dated 7-7-2011 and 11-7-2011 with the petitioner Bank referring the aforesaid Artha Rin Suit and prayed for waiver of interest. But the proposals, being not acceptable, were not considered by the petitioner-bank. The petitioner Bank published auction notice in the 'Daily Janakantha' on 9-2-2011 and the 'Daily Lokshomaj' on 10-2-2011 for selling of the mortgaged property in auction. A number of bids were submitted and highest bid was submitted by one Syed Masudur Rahman and Mosha: Rahima Begum at Taka 36,45,500 which was accepted by the petitioner bank and bid money was deposited by the auctioneers. 

 8. The respondent Nos. 2-4 who were defendant Nos.7ka to 7Ga in Artha Rin Suit 83 of 2004 by filing affidavit-in-opposition opposes the Rule. Their bone of contention is that having receipt of the application under section 19 of Ain, the Adalat rightly restored the suit in its original file and number after setting-aside the ex-parte decree in terms of section 19(4) of Ain and there is no scope in the instant case to initiate a miscellaneous case to consider whether summons were duly served or whether the defendants were prevented by sufficient cause and etc. 

 9. That being so the only question which calls for consideration in this petition is whether under the facts and circumstances of the case the Adalat was justified in allowing the application in the year 2011 under section 19(4) of Ain restoring the suit in its original file and number after setting aside the ex parte decree passed in the year 2004. 

 12. Two aspects have been made abundantly clear in the said provisions of law that an application for restoration of the suit after setting- aside ex-parte decree may be made within 30 days right after passing of the ex-parte decree or from the date of knowledge of the ex-parte decree. The words and phrases in sub-section 2 of section 19 of Ain “একতরফা ডিক্রির তারিখের অথবা উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রি সম্পর্কে অবগত হইবার.....” clearly contemplate two different situations for filing an application for restoration. One right after passing of the ex-pate decree and the other one from the date of knowledge of the ex parte decree as the case may be. The word ‘অথবা’ in the said provision made the two situations disjunctive. Now the question comes whether by implication of sub-section 4 of section 19 of Ain the suit will be automatically restored in both the situations. 

 13. In our interpretation, there is a fine line of understanding in the whole scheme of law in this regard. Right after passing of the ex-parte decree section 19(4) comes into play with all it's trappings i.e. the application if so filed within 30 days shall be automatically restored but certainly not it applies in a case where it has been contended by the defendant that having knowledge of the ex-parte decree the application has been presented. This aspect has not been distinguished under section 19(4) of Ain. When the question of knowledge is the basis for deciding an application for restoration that should be decided in a proper miscellaneous case after hearing the parties of course on evidence. Otherwise, it would be meaningless and also perpetuate an unacceptable trend to allow automatically an application for restoration founded on the basis that right after having knowledge of the ex parte decree the applicant has filed the application for restoration. If that be allowed then one might come with an application for restoration on being having knowledge of the ex parte decree long after passing of the same as it has happened in the instant case. Ex-parte decree was passed in the Year 2004 and the application for restoration was filed 7 Years after on 11-9- 2011. Legislature never intended that by operation of section 19(4) of Ain application of this kind can also be restored without deciding the question of knowledge in a given situation. 

 15. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. The orders impugned against are declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect and accordingly set-aside. The case is sent back to the Adalat to hear and decide the application for restoration of the defendant Nos. 7(ka) to 7 (ga) herein respondents No.2-4 treating the same as a proper miscellaneous case after hearing both sides forthwith.
